title: How to Print Wedding Invitations: Paper, Timing and Proofs
description: Print 5×7 wedding invitations: guest count, proofreading, heavy card stock, print shop vs home, A7 envelopes, when to mail, and ordering a test proof.
summary: Finish your wording first, then print a 5×7 in card with 0.125 in bleed on heavy stock (110 lb / 300 gsm is a common choice for a premium feel). Many couples mail paper invitations about six to eight weeks before the wedding; order a proof, match A7 envelopes, and use a phone share image when you want a quick digital send.

sections.heading: Start with quantity and a frozen guest list
paragraphs: Count households, not just names. One invitation often covers a couple or a family with children. Add ten to fifteen percent extra for last-minute additions, keepsakes and addressing mistakes if your budget allows.

Pause design work until names, the date, the day of the week, the time and the venue match your contract and booking confirmations. A typo in a name is the error printers cannot fix without a full reprint.

If you use the [Wedding Invitation Maker](/create/wedding-invitation-maker), the card uses English wording from a short list of opening and invitation lines, with your typed names, date, venue and optional RSVP line. The maker does not add couple photos, maps or monograms; plan those separately if you need them.

sections.heading: Proofread like a print shop will not
paragraphs: Read the invitation aloud with your partner or a friend who was not involved in typing. Check spelling of names, honorifics, venue names and city lines.

Confirm the RSVP deadline and website URL on the RSVP line match what you will use on your wedding site or reply cards. PiCraft sets the text as part of the artwork, so any change means generating again.
Watch for AI text rendering on unusual names or accents. PiCraft instructs the model to copy your spelling, but a second human read still catches slips before ink hits paper.
items: Date includes the correct year and day of the week.
Time is on its own line if you use a formal phrase such as "four o'clock in the afternoon."
Venue name and city are split the way you want them printed, not crowded into one long line.

sections.heading: Choose paper weight and finish in general terms
paragraphs: Wedding invitations are usually printed on card stock, not thin office paper. PiCraft's wedding checklist suggests heavy card stock, 110 lb (300 gsm) or more, for a premium feel in the hand. Your printer can show swatches; "cover" weight behaves differently from "text" weight on the same label.

Matte finishes hide fingerprints and glare under reception lighting. Slightly textured stocks suit watercolor or botanical art. Gloss can make dark ink pop but shows smudges more easily. Cards with large dark areas, such as the [Art Deco](/create/wedding-invitation-maker/art-deco) style, are the ones to proof on the exact stock you chose.
Ask whether the shop scores folds if you add a separate panel later in another tool. PiCraft exports a flat 5×7 in front design with bleed, not a folded booklet.
after: Full trim, bleed and pixel specs live in the [wedding invitation size](/sizes/wedding-invitation-size) guide, including the 1575×2175 px bleed file at 300 DPI.

sections.heading: Print shop vs home printing
paragraphs: A local or online print shop trims full-bleed PDFs cleanly, runs thick card through commercial presses and can match envelopes in one order. Upload PiCraft's print PDF with 0.125 in bleed and tell them the finished size is 5×7 in after trim. For what bleed means on the file, see [what is bleed in printing](/blog/what-is-bleed-in-printing).

Home inkjet or laser printing works for small guest counts or casual celebrations. Most home devices cannot print edge to edge, so expect a white margin and trim with a paper cutter. Print at 100% scale on card stock your manual allows.
Office copy centers sometimes accept your PDF on a USB drive and print on card stock you buy on the spot. Confirm they will not "fit to page," which changes the dimensions.

sections.heading: Envelopes and mailing
paragraphs: A finished 5×7 in card fits an A7 envelope, which measures 5¼×7¼ in. Order envelopes when you order printing so the paper color and weight feel consistent.

Weigh a completed invitation with any enclosure you plan to include (RSVP card, details insert) before you buy stamps. Non-standard thickness can need extra postage; postal rules vary by country, so check with your local post office.
Addressing can be printed, label-printed or handwritten. If you print addresses, leave adequate margin on the envelope flap side per your printer's template.

sections.heading: When to mail invitations (common timelines)
paragraphs: Etiquette writers and wedding planners often suggest mailing formal invitations about six to eight weeks before the wedding so guests can arrange travel and reply. Destination weddings and holidays are sometimes mailed closer to eight to twelve weeks ahead so guests have more planning time. For a seaside destination, the [beach and coastal](/create/wedding-invitation-maker/beach) style lets you put the town in the city line so guests see where to travel. These are common guidelines, not legal rules; your venue, guest travel and RSVP method matter more than a single fixed date.
Many couples send save-the-date cards months earlier when the date and city are set, then follow with the formal invitation. Digital shares can go out sooner when you only need to hold the date.

Set an RSVP deadline that gives you time to chase replies and share a head count with your caterer. Wedding planning sites often recommend an RSVP date about three to four weeks before the wedding, with at least two weeks before the day for a final count. Put the deadline on the invitation RSVP line or your website.
after: If you mailed late, paperless follow-ups and a clear RSVP link are practical complements; they do not replace posted etiquette advice, but they help you recover time.

sections.heading: Order a test copy before the full run
items: Generate one final design in PiCraft and download the print PDF with bleed.
Order a single proof or the shop's smallest batch on the stock you chose.
Compare color and type size in daylight, not only on your monitor.
Check trim size with a ruler: finished card should be 5×7 in.
Slide the proof into an A7 envelope to confirm fit.
Approve the proof in writing if the shop requires it, then release the full quantity.
after: Keep the approved PDF file name and order number so a reprint matches the first batch.

sections.heading: Digital invitations as a complement
paragraphs: PiCraft also exports a 1080×1500 px share image sized for text messages, WhatsApp, email and vertical stories. It is useful for guests who respond faster on a phone, for reminding people after paper mail goes out, or for events where postage cost is a concern.
The share image is not a bleed print file. Use the PDF or 300 DPI JPG for anything that will be cut on a stack cutter.
For other celebrations that reuse a similar workflow, the [birthday invitation size](/sizes/birthday-invitation-size) guide covers the same 5×7 in print specs and classroom handout tips.

For a lighter touch in the group chat or on a wedding website, a black-and-white [photo booth strip](/create/photo-trend-maker/photo-booth) made from an engagement photo can sit next to the invitation as a fun extra. It is a casual companion image, not a replacement for the formal invitation, and the invitation stays the single source for names, date and venue.

faq.q: What file do I give the printer?
faq.a: Give the 5×7 in print PDF with 0.125 in bleed unless they specify another format. Tell them to trim to 5×7 in finished size.

faq.q: What envelope size fits a 5×7 invitation?
faq.a: A7, measuring 5¼×7¼ in, is the usual match for a 5×7 in card.

faq.q: Can I change the traditional wording on the card?
faq.a: In part. The [Wedding Invitation Maker](/create/wedding-invitation-maker) lets you choose one of four opening lines and one of four invitation lines, all in English. For anything else, use the RSVP field for extra instructions, or edit the downloaded image in another app if you need fully custom wording.

faq.q: How early should RSVPs be due?
faq.a: Many planners suggest three to four weeks before the wedding, with enough time before that for you to follow up with guests who have not replied. Pick a date that fits your caterer's deadline.
